places.name: Neue Nationalgalerie
places.note: Mies's steel and glass temple of 1968, carefully restored by Chipperfield. The empty upper hall is the exhibit.

places.name: Philharmonie
places.note: Scharoun's tent of gold, the orchestra in the middle and terraces of seats around it. Book a lunchtime concert or a tour.

places.name: Neues Museum
places.note: Chipperfield's repair of a bombed museum, scars kept, new brick stitched into old. Nefertiti waits under her own dome.

places.name: Jewish Museum Berlin
places.note: Libeskind's zinc-clad zigzag, cut through with voids you look into but cannot enter. Architecture that makes absence physical.

places.name: Sammlung Boros
places.note: A wartime bunker holding a private collection of contemporary art; the owners live on top. Guided tours only, in small groups; book weeks ahead.

places.name: Hamburger Bahnhof
places.note: A 19th-century railway terminus for contemporary art, with the long shed behind it for the big installations.

places.name: Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church
places.note: Eiermann's 1961 octagon of blue glass blocks beside the bombed spire. Step inside and the light turns everything cobalt.

places.name: Tempelhofer Feld
places.note: A closed airport given back to the city as open field. Runways for cycling and kites, and the biggest sky in Berlin.

places.name: Hufeisensiedlung
places.note: Bruno Taut's horseshoe estate of the 1920s, coloured doors, gardens and all. Modernist housing that is still loved.

places.name: Do You Read Me?!
places.note: A small shop for independent magazines on art, design and fashion. Leave with more than you meant to.

places.name: James-Simon-Galerie
places.note: Chipperfield's colonnaded entrance to Museum Island. Slender white columns and a flight of steps toward the river.

places.name: Altes Museum
places.note: Schinkel's 1830 temple to art, with a domed rotunda of gods. Stand in the colonnade and face the Lustgarten.

places.name: Alte Nationalgalerie
places.note: A temple on a plinth, filled with 19th-century painting. Caspar David Friedrich's room is the quiet centre.

places.name: Gemäldegalerie
places.note: Vermeer, Caravaggio and a room of Rembrandts, rarely crowded. One long enfilade of old masters.

places.name: Berlinische Galerie
places.note: Berlin's own modern art and architecture, in a converted glass warehouse. The yellow letter field outside is part of it.

places.name: C/O Berlin
places.note: Photography in the restored 1950s Amerika Haus. Strong, well-hung exhibitions.

places.name: KW Institute
places.note: A former margarine factory, birthplace of the Berlin Biennale. Dan Graham's glass café pavilion is in the courtyard.

places.name: Helmut Newton Foundation
places.note: Newton's photographs and his rebuilt office, in a former officers' casino by Zoo station.

places.name: Berlin Wall Memorial
places.note: The only stretch of the death strip kept whole, with steel rods marking the line of the Wall. Climb the viewing tower.

places.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
places.note: Eisenman's field of 2,711 concrete stelae on undulating ground. Walk into the middle, alone.

places.name: Reichstag Dome
places.note: Foster's glass dome above the parliament, a spiral ramp around a mirrored cone. Free, but book online.

places.name: Karl-Marx-Allee
places.note: A socialist boulevard of tiled 'workers' palaces' nearly 2 km long. Walk it from Strausberger Platz to Frankfurter Tor.

places.name: Hansaviertel
places.note: The 1957 Interbau estate: Gropius, Niemeyer and Aalto in a park. A modernist open-air exhibition.

places.name: Corbusierhaus
places.note: Le Corbusier's Unité d'habitation for Berlin, a slab on stilts in primary colours.

places.name: Soviet War Memorial, Treptower Park
places.note: A vast Soviet memorial: granite banners, sarcophagi and a colossal soldier on a mound. Overwhelming.

places.name: Teufelsberg
places.note: Cold War listening domes on a hill made of rubble, now covered in graffiti. The forest walk up is half the trip.

places.name: Markthalle Neun
places.note: A 19th-century market hall revived with small producers. Street Food Thursday is the time to go.

places.name: Prater Garten
places.note: Berlin's oldest beer garden, under chestnut trees. Summer only.

places.name: Dussmann das KulturKaufhaus
places.note: Five floors of books and music, open late, with a vertical garden wall in the English bookshop.

places.name: Victoria Bar
places.note: A long, dim cocktail bar for grown-ups, with art on the walls. Exact classic drinks.
